purpose: Ciprofloxacin is an antibiotic used to treat a variety of bacterial infections, including urinary tract infections, skin infections, respiratory infections, and certain types of food poisoning. It is also sometimes used to prevent or treat anthrax exposure. It only works against bacterial infections and will not help with viral illnesses like the common cold or flu.
how_it_works: Ciprofloxacin works by blocking two important enzymes that bacteria need to copy and repair their DNA. Without these enzymes working properly, the bacteria cannot reproduce or survive. This stops the infection from spreading and allows your immune system to clear it from your body.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, and stomach upset. You might also experience headaches, dizziness, or trouble sleeping. Some people notice a skin rash. Taking it with food can help reduce stomach discomfort.
warnings: Ciprofloxacin can rarely cause tendon damage or even tendon rupture, especially in the Achilles tendon — stop taking it and call your doctor right away if you feel tendon pain or swelling. It can also cause nerve damage, mood changes, or worsening of myasthenia gravis. Avoid too much sun exposure as it can make your skin burn more easily. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or under 18, as it is generally avoided in these cases. It can interact with antacids, dairy products, and certain other medications, so take it as directed.
typical_dosing: The typical dose for most adults is 250 mg to 750 mg taken by mouth twice a day, every 12 hours. The exact dose and length of treatment depend on the type and severity of your infection. Always finish the full course of antibiotics even if you start feeling better, and try to take it at the same times each day.
